answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring each identity to climb a vine of sequential attestations from unrelated established peers. Every link demands a unique lotus of original graded work that cannot be reused across clones, and any detected duplicate is pushed off the ledge forfeiting its locked stake. Forging N identities thus requires N independent external chains whose cost grows linearly and cannot be parallelized or bought in bulk, while one honest agent pays only for a single chain.
